newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Finland's Nokia plans solar handset.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Finland's Nokia plans solar handset.

text.p: Europe's largest mobile phone maker Nokia Oy said on Wednesday it would soon launch a handset with a unique solar-powered battery which it claimed would be "the most mobile phone under the sun".

Claiming "another first" in the mobile industry, Nokia said its new 1611 new model, an upgrade of the 1610 handset which is currently targeted at broad consumer markets, could be charged simply by leaving it in a sunny place.

"You don't need plugs or anything like that," said spokeswoman Liisa Nyyssonen. Nokia said it plans to start distributing the new phone in European GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) markets at the end of January.
The 1611 handsets will be in shops in some countries next week, she said.
But the solar batteries will only become available in large volumes in April -- which is about when solar charging would become a serious option, at least at Nokia headquarters in Finland.

With Helsinki under a thick blanket of cloud on Wednesday afternoon, Nyyssonen said solar charging would be unlikely to function. The actual amount of light needed by the new phone would vary but it would work on a partly cloudy day, she said.
"This is one option more for the cellular market," Nyyssonen said, adding that it was hard to predict the potential market size for such a feature.
Analysts agreed, noting the launch comes amid fierce competition in a handset market where the key demands still emphasise long operating times and compactness.
In that context a more arresting feature of the new model might be that Nyyssonen said its standard batteries improve operating times by 10 to 25 percent on the old one.

The standard batteries will have three and a half hours talk time and up to 110 hours standby, and an optional extended battery can stand by for up to nine days with up to seven hours' talk time, Nokia said.
The solar-powered version will give about two hours 20 minutes talk time and up to 73 hours standby, Nyssonen said.

"The solar battery will have marginal impact in the near term, but perhaps longer-term, when people wear mobile phones like watches, the solar option could be significant," one analyst said, requesting anonymity.
